# Objective

- Currently any sort of struct that tracks change detection (either immutably or mutably) has duplicated code. 
- There was a previous attempt to coalesce these into a trait `DetectChanges` however that did not cover the use case for immutable change detection (such as `Res<T>`)

## Solution

- Split the implementation of `DetectChanges` to also have a `SetChanged` trait where the `SetChanged` trait is only implemented for the mutable change detection structs.
pr_comments:

And more specifically, get the value mutably without triggering change detection. 
This is really the only way to fix #2343

issue_context.title: `State::is_changed` is true in every frame, even if the value hasn't changed since last time the system was run.
issue_context.body:
## Bevy version

main-branch

## Operating system & version

Windows 10

## What you did

Added a state and wanted to print out how the state after it is changed.

## What you expected to happen

I expect the printing not to happen on each frame, and only when the state has been changed/set.

## What actually happened


## Additional information

This is very similar to #2275.
comments:
Ahh this seems to be a problem due to the `state_cleaner` system which gets run for each state. 
The problem seems to be that while the inner `state` may not change, there are other fields which may change. 

I think the solution for the problem is going to be to add a way to access a `ResMut` mutably that does _NOT_ trigger change detection.

Here change detection is working properly: the resource `State` changed, even though the state didn't.

A proper fix would probably be:
* rename `State` to `StateHandler`. This `State` isn't the actual state
* add a `state_changed(&self) -> bool` to `StateHandler `

> add a state_changed(&self) -> bool to StateHandler 

I'm not a big fan of this. 
If possible, we should probably use the change detection pattern here and not introduce a new change detection only for states. 

I see two paths:

1) Have a `State<T>` and a `StateHandler<T>`
2) have this work with #2348

I'm slightly in favor of the second choice, however the first one I don't completely hate either. However, it should be noted that the first one adds more complexity in dealing with states.

and

3. rename current `State` resource to `StateHandler`. This makes it obvious that change detection on it won't give you state change detection, and it's semantically correct as the `State` isn't the resource here

I think that the question "did I change state?" is a domain question that need to be answered by a method provided from the state handler, not a platform question provided by change detection on the resource holding it

> rename current State resource to StateHandler. This makes it obvious that change detection on it won't give you state change detection, and it's semantically correct as the State isn't the resource here

I don't dislike this solution, I'm just bothered that when you wrap it in a `ResMut` for example, you still have `is_changed` `set_changed` exposed. 
Regardless of the name of the `StateBikeshed` struct, it's easy for a user to assume that `is_changed` refers to the state in it's entirety. 
Even if you exposed an `is_state_changed` function, this is still ultimately a user trap that we should avoid. 

I'm curious to know @alice-i-cecile or even perhaps @cart views on this. 
For all I know, I'm completely wrong haha and `StateHandler` is the best approach 😄 

I think the simplicity of `State<T>` is best is it make the most semantical sense that `State<T>::is_changed` refers the the changing of the held state. (Since that is the only thing the a user is able to observe from the structure.

I'm in favor of renaming `State` to `StateHandler` (or something to that tune). The current name, as is evident from this issue, is a bit misleading wrt change detection; renaming would completely disambiguate what's happening without a substantial API change, exposing more guts, requiring a new abstraction, or requiring a subversion of API contract suggested in #2348.
I'm in agreement with Ratysz above.

I hit this today (during the jam) 😞

Renaming to `StateHandler` doesn't seem like a perfect fix imo, but it's a trivial change to make and will help alleviate/document the issue a little bit. - would be nice to just merge such a rename in the immediate term and worry about designing a more complex solution later.

For anyone hitting this: the issues with Bevy states will be addressed as part of the Stageless rework ([RFC](https://github.com/bevyengine/rfcs/pull/45)). In the meantime: the [`iyes_loopless`](https://github.com/IyesGames/iyes_loopless/) crate can provide an alternative that works in current Bevy.
